s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of severe headaches and cerebellar syndrome with increased intracranial pressure features
salient_findings: Severe occipital and temporal headaches
Bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
Cerebellar syndrome with ataxia, imbalance, and uncoordinated movements
Bilateral nystagmus and stage I bilateral papilledema
Inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis on brain MRI
key_facts: 44-year-old woman
4-month history of severe headaches
Headaches are paroxysmal and aggravated by changes in position
Associated with bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
Neurological examination shows kinetic and static cerebellar syndrome
Ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, and bilateral nystagmus are present
Stage I bilateral papilledema is present
Routine blood tests are unremarkable
Noncontrast CT of the head shows no abnormalities
Brain MRI shows an inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis
Lesion measures 40 × 31 × 29 mm
Lesion is hypointense on T1-weighted images and heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Lesion shows heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
Lesion fills the foramen of Magendie and exerts mass effect on the medulla
No surrounding edema is seen on FLAIR
Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates increased signal
GRE T2* sequences show no hemorrhage or calcification
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy shows an elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal

shortlist.label: Medulloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches cerebellar vermis location and age of patient

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible match for cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement

shortlist.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common in young adults and can present with cerebellar symptoms

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can occur in cerebellum and present with increased intracranial pressure features

shortlist.label: Cerebellar liponeurocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can present with cerebellar syndrome and increased intracranial pressure

raw.rationale: The lesion's characteristics, such as being hypointense on T1-weighted images and heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images with heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration, along with the presence of an elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal on magnetic resonance spectroscopy, are consistent with a pilocytic astrocytoma, a common cerebellar tumor in adults that can cause increased intracranial pressure and cerebellar syndrome due to its location and mass effect.

rejected.label: Medulloblastoma
rejected.why: Typically more aggressive and common in children

rejected.label: Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Usually shows a strong enhancement pattern and often associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease

rejected.label: Ependymoma
rejected.why: More commonly arises from the ependymal lining of the ventricles or central canal of the spinal cord

rejected.label: Cerebellar liponeurocytoma
rejected.why: Rare tumor with distinct lipid components, not indicated by the provided imaging characteristics
